extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners preparing or prosecuting reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, presenting, examining, and printing amendments, claims, and related materials in reissue patent applications under 37 CFR and MPEP rules. Covers formatting (underlining/bracketing), claim presentation/numbering, examiner procedures, design-reissue special rules, and procedural requirements (oaths, notices, reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: All changes are made vis-à-vis the patent to be reissued
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 CFR 1.173(g), all amendments in the reissue application must be made relative to (i.e. vis-à-vis) the patent specification in effect as of the date of the filing of the reissue application. The patent specification includes the claims and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there was a prior change to the patent (via reexamination certificate, prior reissue, certificate of correction, PTAB trial certificate, etc.), the first amendment of the subject reissue application must be made relative to the patent specification as changed by the prior proceeding. All subsequent amendments must be made relative to the patent specification in effect as of the date of filing of the reissue application, not relative to any prior amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments when underlying patent already has underlining/bracketing (formulas/equations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original (or previously changed) patent includes a formula or equation already having underlining or bracketing as part of the formula, any amendment of such formula/equation should be made by bracketing the entire formula and rewriting and totally underlining the amended formula in the re-presented paragraph or rewritten claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments of segments of a formula or equation should not be made. If the original patent includes bracketing and underlining from an earlier reissue, use double brackets and double underlining in the subject reissue application to identify and distinguish present changes; printed reissue will show double brackets for deletions and boldface for additions. When the reexamination certificate had italics/brackets, present italicized text of the certificate without italics and omit bracketed text from the certificate in the reissue amendment. Canceled claims resulting from a reexamination certificate must be lined through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format for amending original patent paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: To change specification text (e.g., replace a word in a paragraph), submit a copy of the entire paragraph of the specification of the patent being amended with underlining and bracketing, and point out where the paragraph is located (column/line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: 'Replace the paragraph beginning at column 4, line 23 with the following:' followed by the amended paragraph with underlining/bracketing to show changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format for amending original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes to the claims, submit a copy of the entire patent claim with the amendments shown by underlining and bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Amend claim 6 as follows: Claim 6 (Amended). The apparatus of claim [5] 1 wherein the [first] second piezoelectric element...' If the dependency of any original patent claim is to be changed by amendment, it is proper to make that original patent claim dependent upon a later-filed higher-numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: To cancel an original patent claim, in writing, direct cancellation of the patent claim (e.g., 'Cancel claim 6'). To cancel a new claim previously added in the reissue, direct cancellation in writing (e.g., 'Cancel claim 15').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple written direction to cancel the specific claim is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims in reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Each new claim (i.e., a claim not found in the patent, newly presented in the reissue application) should be presented with underlining throughout the claim, including the claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may accept amendments even if claim number is not underlined or status identifiers differ from recommendations, but using status identifier 'New' is recommended so examiners can easily identify new claims. Added claims are numbered beginning with the number next higher than the number of claims in the original patent. If new claims added are later canceled before issuance, the examiner will renumber any remaining new claims in numerical order to follow the number of claims in the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of a new claim (previously presented in reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a 'new claim' must be done by presenting the amended new claim containing the amendatory material, and completely underlining the claim, including the claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presentation cannot contain any bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version of the claim (because changes are vis-à-vis the original patent). Applicant must point out what is changed in the 'Remarks' portion of the amendment. Per 37 CFR 1.173(c), each change made in the claim must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of original patent claims more than once (twice amended claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an original patent claim is amended more than once in a reissue, the later amendment must include the remaining changes previously presented in the first amendment as well as the new changes presented in the later amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words added in the first amendment that are to be deleted in the second amendment (but which never appeared in the original patent) should simply be omitted (not shown in brackets) because they did not appear in the patent. Words added in a later amendment should be underlined. An explanation of deletions/changes should appear in the remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when patent was previously reissued
rubrics_metrics.description: For a reissue application where the patent was previously reissued, double underlining and double bracketing are used in the second reissue application to show amendments made relative to the first reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed second reissue patent will use bold-faced type and double bracketing to indicate further insertions and deletions, respectively, in the second reissue patent. Examples (Re. 23,558 and Re. 28,488) provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when patent was previously reexamined or PTAB certificate issued
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in the reissue application must be presented as if the changes made to the original patent text via the reexamination/PTAB certificate are part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All italicized text of the reexamination certificate is presented in the amendment without italics. Any text found in brackets in the reexamination certificate is omitted in the amendment. A claim canceled by the certificate must be deleted by striking through (lined through), not by surrounding with brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when certificate of correction has issued for the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in the reissue application must be presented as if the changes made via the certificate of correction are part of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All text added by the certificate of correction is presented without italics; text deleted by the certificate is omitted entirely in the amendment. A claim canceled by the certificate of correction must be deleted by striking through (lined through), not surrounded by brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when statutory disclaimer has issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim statutorily disclaimed is no longer in the patent, and such a claim cannot be amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimed claim must be deleted by a direction to strike through the claim (lined through), and not surrounded by brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation when making amendments in a reissue of a previously reissued patent (reissue of a reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a copy of a first reissue patent is presented as the specification of a second reissue application, additions made by the first reissue will already be printed in italics and should remain in such format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need only present additions to the specification/claims in the second reissue as double underlined text. Subject matter to be deleted from the first reissue patent should be presented in the second reissue application within sets of double brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief claim presentation for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements for an appeal brief apply to reissue applications similarly to non-reissue applications, with a difference in presentation of the copy of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims on appeal presented in an appeal brief for a reissue application should include all underlining and bracketing necessary to reflect the changes made to the patent claims during prosecution of the reissue application. Any new claims added in the reissue application should be completely underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: No renumbering of original patent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: No renumbering of the original patent claims is permitted, even if the dependency of a dependent patent claim is changed by reissue so that it becomes dependent on a later higher-numbered claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a dependent claim in a reissue application depends upon a claim which has been canceled, and the dependent claim is not thereafter made dependent upon a pending claim, the dependent claim must be rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and renumbering of new claims upon allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: New claims added during prosecution should be numbered following the highest numbered patent claim, and should be completely underlined. When the reissue application is allowed, claims remaining which are additional to the patent claims should be renumbered in sequence starting with the number next higher than the last claim in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of claims allowed will not necessarily correspond to the number of the last claim in the reissue application as allowed. The 'Total Claims Allowed' box should be consistent with the Notice of Allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim designated for printing in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one claim of an allowable reissue application must be designated for printing in the Official Gazette. Whenever at least one claim has been amended or added in the reissue, the claim(s) designated for printing must include a claim that has been changed or added by the reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A canceled claim is not to be designated as the claim for the Official Gazette. If there is no change in the claims or only cancellations, designate the most representative pending allowed claim for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing proper format for reissue specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reissue application has not been prepared in the indicated manner, the examiner may obtain from applicant a clean copy of the reissue specification prepared in the indicated form, or a proper submission of a previously improperly submitted amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deletions from the original patent are small, the reissue application can be prepared for issue by putting bracketed inserts at appropriate places and numbering added claims. When applicant submits a clean copy or proper submission of an earlier improper amendment, a supplemental reissue declaration should not be provided because format correction does not correct a 35 U.S.C. 251 error in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent application data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All parent application data on the bibliographic data sheet of the original patent file should be present on the bibliographic data sheet of the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue is a continuation reissue of another reissue and there is original-patent parent application data, the examiner should ensure parent application data are properly combined in the specification text and on the bibliographic data sheet, and check combined statement carefully for proper bracketing and underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing references cited and printed in reissue patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should list on a PTO-892 form any reference that was cited during the original prosecution which is again cited/applied in the reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not print in the reissue patent 'References Cited' any reference cited in the patent but not again cited in the reissue application. If applicant wishes to ensure references from the original patent are printed, an IDS in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 should be filed. A patent cannot be reissued solely for adding citations of additional prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment and reissue oath/declaration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary to amend the reissue application to place it in condition for allowance, the examiner may (A) request applicant provide the amendments, or (B) make the amendments with applicant's approval by a formal examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes are made by formal examiner's amendment, the entire paragraphs or claims being amended need to be presented with appropriate markings. The exception for an examiner's amendment in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply to examiner's amendments in reissue applications. For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, if additional defects/errors are corrected after filing the reissue oath/declaration, a supplemental oath/declaration is not required; however if all previously identified errors are no longer relied upon, applicant must explicitly identify an error being relied upon for reissue (conspicuously and clearly, complying with 35 U.S.C. 251). For filings before that date, a supplemental oath/declaration will be required to correct an 'error' under 35 U.S.C. 251; examiner should telephone applicant to request the supplemental oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final review of the reissue application by the examiner (Examiner Reissue Checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before forwarding a reissue application to the Technology Center (TC) Training Quality Assurance Specialist (TQAS) or Supervisory Patent Reexamination Specialist (SPRS) for final review, the examiner should complete and initial an Examiner Reissue Checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the checklist should be available from the TQAS or SPRS. Completion/initialing is required prior to final review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue monitoring and TQAS review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications assigned to Technology Centers are monitored and reviewed by the appropriate TQAS at several stages during prosecution to check that reissue-unique practice and procedure have been carried out and to perform patentability review samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TQASs must set terminal-specific status flags when a new reissue application enters the TC (enter number in Office-wide grouping) so TQAS sees assignment and can instruct examiner. The TQAS must remove the flag before a Notice of Allowance or issue revision transaction can be entered to ensure final TQAS review when appropriate. Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) reissue applications are monitored and reviewed by SPRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design reissue: expedited examination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Design reissue applications requesting expedited examination and complying with 37 CFR 1.155 are examined with priority and undergo expedited processing throughout prosecution, including appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reissue and request are processed by OPAP and forwarded to Design TC Director's Office. If 1.182 waiver is granted, the Design Group begins expedited examination promptly; decision under 1.182 will require no Notice of Allowance be mailed until after 2 months from publication in the Official Gazette, to allow consideration of protests filed under 37 CFR 1.291.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design reissue fees and claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design reissue application fee is set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(e). A search fee (1.16(n)) and an examination fee (1.16(r)) are also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The additional fees in 1.16(h) and 1.16(i) do not apply for a design reissue application because more than one claim is not permitted in a design application pursuant to the last sentence of 37 CFR 1.153(a). The fee for issuing a design reissue patent is set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple design reissue applications and restriction/divisional practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A design reissue application can be filed based on the 'error' of failing to include a design for a patentably distinct segregable part or subcombination of the claimed design, if filed within two years of issuance (considered a broadening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction will be required under 37 CFR 1.176(b); the added segregable part will be held constructively non-elected and withdrawn. Examiner should suggest filing a divisional design reissue application directed to constructively non-elected subject matter. Action in original reissue will be suspended pending divisional. If divisional found allowable, a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is required to waive 1.153 to permit rejoining of designs into single claim for issuance. Filing is improper if original application included the segregable part and a restriction was made but applicant failed to file a divisional before issue of original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between design and utility patents via reissue prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: A design patent cannot be converted to a utility patent via reissue, and a utility patent cannot be converted to a design patent via reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions are improper because (a) the design patent disclosure is not directed to how the invention is made/used and conversion would introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 251/new matter/enablement/112 issues), (b) conversion could improperly extend patent term or exempt maintenance fees, and (c) no statutory basis exists to permit these conversions. Examiner should consider rejections based on new matter, lack of enablement, and/or lack of description where such conversions are attempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed reissue patent heading and printing conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The specifications of reissue patents will be printed to show changes over the original patent text by enclosing any material omitted by the reissue in heavy brackets [ ] and printing material added by the reissue in italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The printed reissue patent specification will carry the Office-added heading: 'Matter enclosed in heavy brackets [ ] appears in the original patent but forms no part of this reissue specification; matter printed in italics indicates the additions made by reissue.' Examiners should ensure specification is in proper form for printing, carefully check entry of all amendments so changes directed by applicant are accurately printed. Matter added by amendment in the reissue that is later canceled should be crossed through, not bracketed. All claims of the original patent should appear in the reissue patent, with canceled patent claims being enclosed in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissue under 35 U.S.C. 252
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of the reissued patent, surrender of the original patent takes effect; every reissued patent shall have the same effect and operation in law as if originally granted in the amended form, with certain continuity for substantially identical claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue does not abridge rights of persons who, prior to reissue, made, purchased, offered to sell, used, or imported the patented thing; courts may provide for continued manufacture/use/sale or equitable terms for investments made before the grant of the reissue. The reissued patent, to the extent its claims are substantially identical to the original patent, constitutes a continuation with effect from the date of the original patent.
